author: Ifmyante
text:
Thanks for the support and kind words FB

It's no surprise that some of the best associate traders we have are
those who found RTM at the beginning of their trading journeys.

Their heads hadn't been stuffed with all the misinformation so many of the rest of us had to endure.

We showed them the reality of the Emperor's new clothes and they saw straight away that he was buck naked!.

Reading the market and trading it are very simple indeed, once you
unlearn all the BS you've been taught to believe over the years.

I have really high expectations of new traders who take this course. Its
 structure is such that, lesson by lesson, it should layer understanding
 upon understanding, so that by the time the students get to learning
the rules they'll use in trading, they'll understand exactly why those
rules exist.

I also have great hopes for the students who've been through the mill.
If they can find a way to completely clear their minds, and take the
first class as if they had known nothing of trading before, there's a
great chance for them to at last see how truly simple it can be

I'm absolutely itching to see the transformation of the first RTM Academy Graduates. Something tells me we all are :)

author: Ifmyante
text:
Hi All

We're hoping to open the doors to the RTM Academy on Monday morning,
although we haven't finished testing the new platform we intend to use
for the course.

But even if the platform's not ready, we'll get the lessons out there one way or another.

I really don't know what the lessons schedule will be; our Beta
Students' progress will guide me on that. I want the scheduling to be
mindful of the time constraints of the different students, yet I don't

and on to the next section the week after.

So, get your pencils sharpened, and we'll see you in class on Monday :)

author: Ifmyante
text:
Hi Forethan

I abhor discussing money, so I shan't.

As many of you already know, I lost my family due to all the time I spent helping people for free.

I had locked myself away day and night for so long working out how the
market works, that of course it depleted the patience of my love. Then
what did I do once I had learned enough to make us very rich? I opened a
 website, where I spent day and night teaching people what I'd laboured
over for so long.

After such a cost in time and money (yes, I was trading live from the start ), I was now giving it all away for free! Well, of course I was asking for trouble!

I had the opportunity to fix it, by not opening RTM, and focusing solely
 on family and trading. But instead, I went ahead with it, and by the
time RTM went live, I was in my third day of homelessness. I'll never
forget New Years Day, 2013, I can assure you.

It's now exactly seven months since RTM opened (7 mths 2 days since I
lost my home), and I'm about to start giving focused lessons on all I've
 learned, spending alot of time on each student who comes with me.

But now I know the value (and the cost to me) of what it is I'm giving,
and if the students are in any doubt about it before we begin, they'll
know it once we're done.

Now, should I do this for free? Should I make deals over my time and
experience? Should I devalue myself and all I've been through?

It's simply in my nature to learn and to share what I've learned. But
it's also in my nature to live with my family, whom I miss more than
most can ever imagine,

Is it wrong to hope, that if I can show that all the time and effort
I've put into teaching has actually been of some benefit to my family,
that I may actually get them back? Maybe even regain the respect of the
one person I most want the respect of?

I'm sorry Forethan, this rant wasn't in any way directed at you. It's
just that I have no filter on which parts of the truth I should leave
unsaid

So, back to business:

Regarding guaranteeing success; All I can do is guarantee that I'll
teach how the market works, and will help each student choose the
trading plans that'll work best for them. All that's important, and none
 of what's unimportant will be in the course, and if the students take
this to heart, and follow their plans with patience and understanding,
they will have every possible chance of getting to the top of this
business.

I cannot guarantee that students will stick to the plans. I cannot
guarantee that students won't get the sudden urge to try an MA crossover
 system ten minutes after graduation, and blow their accounts in a week!
 I cannot guarantee that some students won't do exactly the opposite of
what they've been advised.There are so many variables within each
student that it's impossible for me to guarantee their actions.

Best

If

Hi IF, sorry about the missed trade, such a pity! This however reminded
me of a question that I've been wondering about. First of all I believe
your trade was based on the H4 supply zone below, correct me if I'm
wrong!

I've always been curious about utilizing the LTFs to pin point entries
to the pip. Your ability to read the M1 chart to enter trades with the
tightest stop possible is undoubtedly uncanny, however do you frequently
 experience missed opportunities because of this? I personally have seen
 many trades take off before hitting the deepest M1 FTR that would
provide the best RR possible, which makes me wonder when and how you use
 the M1 to pin point your entries. Lets take this EJ H4 zone for
example, I've labelled a couple of places where price could have
reversed from, why were you sure that price would break past all these?

Also, doesn't it worry you if price actually went that deep into a zone?
 Personally whenever price goes really deep into a zone I traded, odds
are that I'll get stopped out :P

Oh ya, considering that it was just before NFP, weren't you afraid that
such a tight stop would get taken out as market makers might hunt stops
during the low liquidity period before a major news release?

Hope you don't mind the barrage of questions!
